properties.Period / Event: Composition of the Ṛgveda
properties.Description: Composition of the Ṛgveda; √yuj appears in the sense of yoking (chariots; later the mind) alongside ecstatic seer figures (kesin; muni) — Earliest vocabulary layer of the tradition; no systematic yoga yet

properties.Period / Event: Atharvaveda compiled
properties.Description: Atharvaveda compiled; hymns on prāṇa (vital breath) and the ritual ascetic vrātyas — Early breath and asceticism ideas that later feed prāṇāyāma and tapas

properties.Period / Event: Brāhmaṇas and Āraṇyakas interiorize ritual
properties.Description: Brāhmaṇas and Āraṇyakas interiorize ritual; tapas (heat; austerity) and breath control become central practices — Shift from external sacrifice to internal discipline

properties.Period / Event: Early prose Upaniṣads teach ātman-brahman identity and meditation as…
properties.Description: Early prose Upaniṣads teach ātman-brahman identity and meditation as inner sacrifice — Philosophical ground for later yoga goals (liberation through knowledge)

properties.Period / Event: Kaṭha Upaniṣad gives an early definition of yoga as firm holding of…
properties.Description: Kaṭha Upaniṣad gives an early definition of yoga as firm holding of the senses (chariot metaphor) — First strong use of 'yoga' as a discipline of mind and senses

properties.Period / Event: Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad gives early instructions on posture and breath…
properties.Description: Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad gives early instructions on posture and breath within a devotional (Rudra-Śiva) frame — Early mention of body alignment and breath in meditation

properties.Period / Event: Maitrī Upaniṣad describes a six-limbed (ṣaḍaṅga) yoga
properties.Description: Maitrī Upaniṣad describes a six-limbed (ṣaḍaṅga) yoga — Precursor to Patañjali's eight limbs

properties.Period / Event: Mahābhārata includes the Bhagavad Gītā (karma- jñāna- and bhakti-yoga
properties.Description: Mahābhārata includes the Bhagavad Gītā (karma- jñāna- and bhakti-yoga; yoga as equanimity) and Sāṃkhya-Yoga material in the Mokṣadharma — Yoga becomes a broad path concept beyond meditation (Gītā 2.48 samatvaṃ yoga ucyate)

properties.Period / Event: Patañjali's Yoga Sūtras compiled (~195 sūtras in four pādas)
properties.Description: Patañjali's Yoga Sūtras compiled (~195 sūtras in four pādas); eight-limbed (aṣṭāṅga) path; Sāṃkhya metaphysics — Foundational classical yoga text; teaches a steady seat for meditation rather than a posture repertoire (YS 2.46)

properties.Period / Event: Īśvarakṛṣṇa's Sāṃkhyakārikā systematizes the 25 tattvas and the three…
properties.Description: Īśvarakṛṣṇa's Sāṃkhyakārikā systematizes the 25 tattvas and the three guṇas — Standard source for the puruṣa-prakṛti-guṇa framework

properties.Period / Event: Vyāsa's Yoga Bhāṣya becomes the standard commentary on the Yoga Sūtras
properties.Description: Vyāsa's Yoga Bhāṣya becomes the standard commentary on the Yoga Sūtras — Earliest extant commentary; Sūtras and Bhāṣya may have circulated as one work

properties.Period / Event: Vācaspati Miśra writes the Tattvavaiśāradī sub-commentary on the Yoga…
properties.Description: Vācaspati Miśra writes the Tattvavaiśāradī sub-commentary on the Yoga Bhāṣya — Major interpretive layer for later Yoga-Sāṃkhya scholarship

properties.Period / Event: Tantric traditions elaborate mantra
properties.Description: Tantric traditions elaborate mantra; mudrā; cakras; nāḍīs and kuṇḍalinī; Kashmir Śaivism develops — Subtle-body models later absorbed into haṭha yoga

properties.Period / Event: Nāth Siddha ascetics develop haṭha yoga techniques (bandhas
properties.Description: Nāth Siddha ascetics develop haṭha yoga techniques (bandhas; mudrās; breath retention) aimed at stabilizing bindu and breath; very few āsanas taught — Origin of haṭha practice; posture is a minor limb

properties.Period / Event: Svātmārāma compiles the Haṭha Yoga Pradīpikā
properties.Description: Svātmārāma compiles the Haṭha Yoga Pradīpikā; teaches 15 āsanas plus ṣaṭkarma; prāṇāyāma; mudrā; samādhi — Most influential premodern haṭha manual

properties.Period / Event: Later haṭha compendia expand posture lists: Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā (32…
properties.Description: Later haṭha compendia expand posture lists: Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā (32 āsanas); Śiva Saṃhitā; Haṭharatnāvalī; Jogapradīpyakā (1737; 84 āsanas) — Posture repertoire grows but stays mostly seated and floor-based
properties.Texts: Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā; Śiva Saṃhitā; Haṭharatnāvalī; Jogapradīpyakā

properties.Period / Event: Theosophical Society founded (1875)
properties.Description: Theosophical Society founded (1875); Orientalist translations and Western esotericism recast yoga; haṭha yogis often dismissed as 'fakirs' by reformers — Sets conditions for the modern reframing of yoga

properties.Period / Event: Swami Vivekananda at the Parliament of the World's Religions (Chicago…
properties.Description: Swami Vivekananda at the Parliament of the World's Religions (Chicago 1893); Rāja Yoga published 1896 reframes Patañjali for a Western audience — Starts modern transnational yoga; emphasizes meditation over postures

properties.Period / Event: Indian physical culture merges with European gymnastics and…
properties.Description: Indian physical culture merges with European gymnastics and YMCA-style fitness; modern postural yoga takes shape — Scholars (Singleton; Alter) describe modern posture practice as a hybrid
properties.Key figures: Bishnu Charan Ghosh; Shri Yogendra; Swami Kuvalayananda

properties.Period / Event: Shri Yogendra founds The Yoga Institute in Bombay (Santa Cruz)
properties.Description: Shri Yogendra founds The Yoga Institute in Bombay (Santa Cruz); visits the US in 1919 — Begins institutional householder yoga in India

properties.Period / Event: Paramahansa Yogananda arrives in the US and founds Self-Realization…
properties.Description: Paramahansa Yogananda arrives in the US and founds Self-Realization Fellowship; Kriya Yoga reaches the West — Early large-scale Indian yoga teaching in America

properties.Period / Event: Swami Kuvalayananda founds Kaivalyadhama (Lonavla) and the journal…
properties.Description: Swami Kuvalayananda founds Kaivalyadhama (Lonavla) and the journal Yoga Mīmāṃsā; laboratory research on yoga — Start of scientific yoga research

properties.Period / Event: Krishnamacharya teaches in the Mysore Palace yogaśālā under the…
properties.Description: Krishnamacharya teaches in the Mysore Palace yogaśālā under the Maharaja; publishes Yoga Makaranda (1934); dynamic vinyāsa sequences emerge — Root of the Ashtanga; Iyengar and Viniyoga lines

properties.Period / Event: Swami Sivananda founds the Divine Life Society in Rishikesh
properties.Description: Swami Sivananda founds the Divine Life Society in Rishikesh — Source of the Sivananda lineage (Vishnudevananda; Satchidananda; Satyananda)

properties.Period / Event: Autobiography of a Yogi published
properties.Description: Autobiography of a Yogi published — Brings yoga and Kriya to a mass Western readership

properties.Period / Event: Indra Devi opens a yoga studio in Hollywood (1947)
properties.Description: Indra Devi opens a yoga studio in Hollywood (1947); K. Pattabhi Jois founds the Ashtanga Yoga Research Institute in Mysore (1948) — Yoga reaches celebrity circles; Ashtanga formally institutionalized

properties.Period / Event: Yehudi Menuhin meets B.K.S. Iyengar (1952) and brings him to the West…
properties.Description: Yehudi Menuhin meets B.K.S. Iyengar (1952) and brings him to the West (1954) — Iyengar's international teaching begins

properties.Period / Event: Swami Vishnudevananda opens the first Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centre…
properties.Description: Swami Vishnudevananda opens the first Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centre (Montréal) — Spreads Sivananda Yoga across North America

properties.Period / Event: Television yoga: Richard Hittleman's Yoga for Health (from 1961) and…
properties.Description: Television yoga: Richard Hittleman's Yoga for Health (from 1961) and Lilias Folan's Lilias; Yoga and You (from c. 1970) — Mass-market home yoga in the US

properties.Period / Event: B.K.S. Iyengar's Light on Yoga published
properties.Description: B.K.S. Iyengar's Light on Yoga published; Swami Satchidananda opens the Integral Yoga Institute in New York — Defining reference for modern āsana practice

properties.Period / Event: Counterculture era: Beatles visit Maharishi in Rishikesh (1968)
properties.Description: Counterculture era: Beatles visit Maharishi in Rishikesh (1968); Satchidananda opens Woodstock (1969); Yogi Bhajan founds 3HO (1969) — Yoga becomes a mainstream Western spiritual and wellness movement
properties.Key figures: Maharishi Mahesh Yogi; Swami Satchidananda; Yogi Bhajan

properties.Period / Event: Himalayan Institute founded (1971)
properties.Description: Himalayan Institute founded (1971); Iyengar institute in Pune opens (1975); Pattabhi Jois first teaches in the US (1975); Yoga Journal founded (1975) — Institutions and publishing consolidate the Western scene
properties.Key figures: Swami Rama; B.K.S. Iyengar; K. Pattabhi Jois

properties.Period / Event: Bikram Choudhury opens a studio in Beverly Hills (heated 26-posture…
properties.Description: Bikram Choudhury opens a studio in Beverly Hills (heated 26-posture sequence) — Origin of branded hot yoga

properties.Period / Event: T.K.V. Desikachar founds Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in Chennai
properties.Description: T.K.V. Desikachar founds Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in Chennai — Individualized therapeutic Viniyoga lineage

properties.Period / Event: Studio-yoga boom: Jivamukti (1984)
properties.Description: Studio-yoga boom: Jivamukti (1984); Power Yoga (1995); Anusara (1997); Yoga Alliance (1999) — Vinyasa and hybrid styles go mainstream in the US
properties.Key figures: Sharon Gannon; David Life; Beryl Bender Birch; John Friend

properties.Period / Event: Critical history of modern yoga: De Michelis's A History of Modern…
properties.Description: Critical history of modern yoga: De Michelis's A History of Modern Yoga (2004); Alter's Yoga in Modern India (2004); Singleton's Yoga Body (2010) — Reframes modern postural yoga as a twentieth-century hybrid
properties.Key figures: Elizabeth De Michelis; Joseph Alter; Mark Singleton
properties.Texts: A History of Modern Yoga; Yoga in Modern India; Yoga Body

properties.Period / Event: United Nations proclaims 21 June International Day of Yoga (Dec 2014)
properties.Description: United Nations proclaims 21 June International Day of Yoga (Dec 2014); first observed 2015 — Global institutional recognition

properties.Period / Event: Teacher-misconduct reckonings (e.g. Bikram
properties.Description: Teacher-misconduct reckonings (e.g. Bikram; Anusara; Ashtanga; 3HO); decolonization and appropriation debates; trauma-informed yoga and yoga therapy grow — Ethics and inclusion now part of many trainings; verify specifics before citing
